findings.fact: request_terminate attempts kill; terminate aborts I/O tasks and drops the waiter JoinHandle without aborting/joining the native waiter. The waiter separately completes child.wait then records exit and sends the native result. No ordering guarantees that these observations are ready when terminate returns.

The server returns after request_terminate; watch_exit separately receives the native result, retains custody, then publishes the process exit. RemoteProcessSession terminate discards the response body and returns only success/error. An ACK cannot authorize has_exited.

terminate_confirmed requests termination then performs one immediate snapshot. If the existing observer has not committed exit yet it marks a sticky observation failure and cancels the polling token. Manager returns false before owner removal. A healthy in-flight native observation is therefore treated like failed observation.

Both Local and ExecServer already publish native exit/failure into the retained watch::ProcessState. A fix can await this same owner-bound state and does not need a second read RPC, synthetic code, polling sleep or repeated termination requests.

The current terminate APIs carry process_id and return bool without an explicit confirmation deadline. Existing EARLY_EXIT_GRACE_PERIOD belongs to startup and is not an established termination budget. The 2s test timeout is a watchdog, not a production policy.

Current tests preserve ACK-only indeterminate, observation-loss, existing real exit and control-error semantics. Success coverage has native exit committed before terminate returns/ACK release. There is no deterministic case with ACK first and a later valid native exit while confirmation is awaiting it.

bounded_repair_requirements: Choose an explicit owner-level finite confirmation deadline/budget; do not silently recycle startup/output budgets or extend original test timeouts.
Issue termination once. Keep the existing observer alive and wait only for retained same-owner ProcessState changes. Do not infer exit from ACK, Closed, input refusal, cancellation or output EOF.
Use watch state/changed sequencing that cannot lose a wake. Success requires actual has_exited; preserve any actual numeric code and allow legitimately observed exited-without-code.
If a real observation failure occurs, return its first message promptly unless a native exit is already retained; preserve current control-failure semantics.

At deadline perform a final coherent state decision. If still unobserved, retain failure/ownership and return indeterminate; never remove the registry owner or claim exit based solely on elapsed time. Do not overwrite a concurrently retained real exit.
Preserve manager Arc identity recheck, initial_exec_command_active behavior and cleanup ordering.

Keep every existing assertion. Add deterministic barrier-based coverage for ACK before native exit, Local driver result after terminate request, and expired/no-exit outcome; retain existing ACK-only and observation-loss tests without longer watchdogs.
adjacent_ordering_caution: Local waiters currently set exit_status before writing exit_code and sending the oneshot. Any new confirmation logic should use the retained native-result watch when waiting, not assume those separate fields form an atomic numeric-exit snapshot. This review does not propose an unrelated PTY rewrite.
evidence_limits: The original failure log contains the false boolean, not an internal scheduling trace. The exact scheduling of that execution is unmeasured; the source proves an allowed race consistent with the observed failure.
No production code, test assertions, timeout or native environment was changed. No Rust build/test or live process probe was run by this reviewer.
This report proposes bounded semantics for review; it does not choose an unsupported numeric production deadline or claim a candidate passes.
